{
  "trigger": "The paper proposes a theoretical modification to a standard algorithm (e.g., removing EMA or changing loss weighting) and validates it primarily on small-scale datasets or simple backbones.",
  "review_heuristic": "Verify if the experimental scale (dataset size, model complexity) is sufficient to support the generalizability claims of the theoretical contribution. If the validation is limited to small benchmarks (e.g., CIFAR-10, VGG11), flag the lack of evidence for scalability to complex architectures or large-scale datasets (e.g., ImageNet, ResNet-50).",
  "evidence_to_check": "Check the experimental section for the specific datasets and backbone architectures used. Compare these against the state-of-the-art standards for the proposed method's domain. Look for ablations or additional experiments on larger scales if the main results are on small data.",
  "failure_mode": "Overclaiming robustness or scalability based on small-scale validation, where the method might fail or degrade in performance on larger, more complex models or datasets.",
  "why_it_matters": "Theoretical insights often assume idealized conditions; empirical validation on small scales may not capture the dynamics of large-scale training (e.g., optimization landscape differences, data diversity), leading to a gap between theoretical promise and practical utility.",
  "reviewer_dimension": "QUAL"
}
